transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole, Riley Zhang (Redwood), Maya Patel, Diego Ramos, Lena Cho (Novastream)

Summary: quick discovery on embeddings + reranking needs, current stack uses Pinecone, exploring Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for hybrid search and throughput needs. Action items and next steps captured at end.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for joining, umm, quick intros — I'm Avery, AE at Redwood Inference. Riley and Samir from my side — Riley is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Maya: hi, Maya here, head of search at Novastream, Diego's on the call who runs our vector infra, Lena is on for architecture questions.
[00:18] Riley: nice to meet you all, we'll do a quick set of questions to understand your production goals and then talk about options.
[00:35] Diego: cool, quick note, apologies if audio is a bit spotty, we're on a, uh, campus VPN.
[00:42] Avery: no problem. high-level — what's your current setup for embeddings and reranking?
[00:57] Maya: so currently we generate embeddings with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, store vectors in Pinecone, dimension is 1536, we do hybrid search — BM25 + vector scoring for rerank. Latency targets are 100-150ms p50 for our search front-end. Throughput varies, peak is around 2k QPS during campaigns, baseline ~300 QPS.
[01:20] Riley: got it. what's your cost pain right now? CPU/GPU for re-embedding? pinecone storage?
[01:28] Maya: pinecone costs doing ok but the rerank stage on our side is heavy — we currently do a two-stage approach: ANN recall from Pinecone then an LLM-rerank step hosted in our infra. That LLM step is expensive and brittle. We're evaluating moving rerank to a managed inference layer.
[01:45] Avery: makes sense; users want consistent latency and predictable cost. are you considering Redwood Hosted (quick to iterate), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem)?
[01:58] Lena: we have data residency requirements for EU users and PCI adjacent flows, so Private or Dedicated with VPC peering looks likely, but we'd like to understand tradeoffs.
[02:10] Diego: also curious about throughput and dimensionality — if we drop from 1536 to 768 dims how much accuracy loss we see, and how that maps to compute.
[02:23] Riley: great, two threads — infra and embeddings. On infra: Hosted is fastest to get started, but Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable latency SLOs; Private adds customer-managed networking and KMS. For throughput: our Dedicated pools can be configured to sustain tens of thousands of tokens/sec per pool depending on model and quantization. We'll share sample numbers.
[02:47] Maya: when you say "model" here you mean the reranker model — are you recommending an encoder-only embed model vs cross-encoder for rerank?
[02:57] Riley: good question — typical pattern: use an embedding model (bi-encoder) for ANN recall, then a cross-encoder or a small re-ranker for final ranking. Cross-encoders are more accurate but higher latency; another approach is to use a small LLM as a reranker with structured prompts, lower token counts. We often suggest doing a hybrid: tuned embeddings + a light-weight reranker.
[03:20] Diego: we currently do a cross-encoder for rerank (it's 1.5B param) and it's pretty costly. If we swapped to a smaller re-ranker, what's the expected throughput change?
[03:33] Riley: ballpark — on a single GPU, a 1.5B cross-encoder might handle a few hundred qps if you do full cross-attention across 50 candidates; a dedicated batch-optimized kernel can push that. Using our batching + KV cache for session workloads helps. If you move to a distilled reranker (like 220M), you can get multi-thousand QPS per GPU.
[03:55] Maya: hmm ok. about vector DB integration — does Redwood have built-in vector store or do you pair with Pinecone/Milvus?
[04:05] Avery: Redwood integrates with common vector DBs — Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate — and you can also use our native quickstore for small pilots. Integration is via our SDKs and connector patterns; we can also push as part of a managed workflow.
[04:20] Diego: any gotchas on schema? we use metadata filtering a lot and we need hybrid search (ann + bm25).
[04:28] Riley: metadata filters are first-class — our recall stage supports vector + metadata filters; for hybrid you can combine BM25 external recall and use the vector-based second stage or vice versa. We saw some clients keep BM25 in their existing ES/Opensearch and call Redwood for rerank only.
[04:48] Lena: encryption — we need KMS integration and audit logs for compliance. How mature is that?
[04:55] Avery: we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can integrate with enterprise KMS via bring-your-own-key for enterprise tiers. Audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and retention controls are supported. We'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 docs.
[05:12] Maya: perfect, please send the SOC 2 and details on retention. Also curious about data in flight and at rest encryption specifics.
[05:21] Riley: will do.
[05:30] Diego: performance tests — can we run a benchmark with our sample corpus? we'll need a test harness and a plan to measure rerank accuracy (MRR/NDCG) as well as latency percentiles.
[05:41] Riley: yes, we have a benchmark kit; we'll need dataset share and an S3 bucket or access credentials. We can run hosted tests for small scale or spin up a Dedicated pool for more realistic numbers.
[05:56] Avery: what about dimensionality choices — Maya mentioned 1536; have you tried 768?
[06:06] Maya: we ran 768 once, saw about 3-4% drop in relevance on some vertical queries. But cost savings were substantial. We're trying to quantify tradeoffs.
[06:16] Riley: that's typical; we recommend running a lift test: compare P@10/MRR on your evaluation set with several dims and quantization profiles. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization + embeddings combos and estimate unit cost.
[06:30] Diego: question on hybrid search — we sometimes need semantic boosting for recency; can Redwood incorporate time decay in rerank pipeline?
[06:40] Riley: yes, you can inject recency features as metadata and have the reranker incorporate those signals; or you can reweight candidate scores pre-rerank. We also support fielded vectors and per-candidate metadata to let the model reason about recency.
[06:58] Maya: what's the timeline to get a POC up and running? we need results for exec review in three weeks.
[07:06] Avery: tight but doable — hosted evaluation within 3-5 days if you give us the corpus and API keys; Dedicated POC provisioning is a bit longer (2-3 weeks) for reserved pool spin-up depending on capacity. Private/on-prem depends on network approvals.
[07:18] Lena: ok. also pricing — is it per-token for rerank or per-query? Our rerank prompt is small but cross-encoder inputs can blow up token counts if you concatenate 50 candidates.
[07:29] Riley: we price hosted per-token for generative/rerank operations and per-embedding unit for embedding generation; Dedicated is typically reserved capacity plus usage. For cross-encoder style rerank we can provide guidance on batching and chunking to reduce billing impact — e.g., use candidate pruning to limit number of matches fed to the cross-encoder. We'll send sample cost models.
[07:52] Diego: any limits on candidate count for rerank? we can supply 100 candidates in the worst case.
[07:58] Riley: functionally you can send many candidates but latency/cost scales linearly; typical pattern is recall 100 -> rerank top 50 -> final top 10. For large scale, consider a multi-stage pipeline with a cheaper reranker first.
[08:16] Maya: security follow-up: audit log retention and access controls — do you provide per-customer retention windows?
[08:25] Avery: yes, retention windows configurable on Dedicated/Private; Hosted has tiers. We'll include options in the security doc.
[08:35] Diego: another question — is there an SDK for batching pipelines so we can run candidate recall + batch rerank calls?
[08:42] Riley: yes, our SDK supports multi-call workflows and streaming responses for partial rerank; also server-side batching config for Dedicated to improve throughput.
[08:56] Maya: okay, can we do a quick sketch of the POC plan?
[09:01] Riley: sure — step 1: you share sample corpus and eval set. Step 2: we run an initial hosted pilot to compare your current cross-encoder vs Redwood's suggested reranker/quantization (A/B). Step 3: run Dedicated benchmark if results look promising. Step 4: iterate on thresholds and caching.
[09:18] Maya: timeline: we need initial numbers for exec in 3 weeks, so hosted pilot first.
[09:24] Avery: agree. we'll follow up with files and credentials.
[09:30] Riley: quick note on names — sometimes the transcript or docs may show Redwood product names slightly off, e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" is fine but sometimes auto-transcribers write "Redwood Dedicate".
[09:40] Maya: (laughs) noted.
[09:44] -- 16:20 small side thread on network peering, options listed --
[10:10] Lena: we have a question about SLAs — can you commit to p99 latency targets?
[10:18] Avery: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed targets depending on the plan; for Hosted we have published SLOs for enterprise tiers. We'll include specifics.
[10:28] Diego: curious about monitoring — do you capture token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?
[10:34] Riley: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency, per-model dashboards, traces, and error analysis.
[10:42] Maya: great. anything else?
[10:45] Avery: final recap — Avery to send pricing and security pack; Riley to prepare benchmark plan and coordinate with Diego; Maya to share dataset and current vector schema; schedule technical deep dive for next week.
[11:02] Maya: thanks all.
[11:05] Avery: thanks, we'll follow-up via email with links: security whitepaper (https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf), Dedicated pricing deck (link in email), and benchmark template (shared drive).

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; speakers sometimes overlapped. References: sample docs will be attached separately rather than pasted here.
